detail:
The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) describes attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) as a developmental disorder marked by persistent symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. NIMH notes symptoms begin in childhood, can interfere with daily life including social relationships and school or work performance, and often continue into the teen years and adulthood, so many adults also have the disorder.

Based on the specific symptoms, NIMH describes three types of ADHD: predominantly inattentive, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive, and combined. Symptoms can include difficulty paying attention, keeping on task, or staying organized, moving around at inappropriate times or talking excessively, and interrupting or having trouble waiting for a turn. Researchers are not sure what causes ADHD, although NIMH notes many studies suggest genes play a large role. Diagnosis in the sources is made by a clinician from the symptom pattern, its duration, and evidence that symptoms began before age 12.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about ADHD symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: NIMH describes ADHD as a developmental disorder of persistent inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity beginning in childhood and often continuing into adulthood, diagnosed by a clinician from the symptom pattern in one of three types.
takeaways: adhd involves persistent inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, nimh describes
symptoms begin in childhood and often continue into adulthood
clinicians describe three types based on the symptom pattern
title: ADHD: inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity from childhood
